title: Four-Wave Identification of First-Post Treatment Effects on the Treated with an Absorbing State
banked_reason: Banked downgraded on 2026-09-09 during Lean formalization: the derivation had passed review at field tier, but the cold D0.5.G re-score under the projected-paper-score rule gave 7.6 and tier subfield, and the run was banked on that tier; the run did not fail and is a re-raise candidate.
tldr: This ExactID result uses four observed waves and fixed known \(2\leq J\leq m\).  Four corner slices determine the spectral basis; \(2m-1\) fixed selected anchor-star minors transport it across active anchors; and the remaining observable \(A_{xy}\) slices recover non-anchor transitions without additional rank requirements.  The map identifies active component sublaws, type contributions, at-risk effects, and the aggregate first-post ATT despite a common absorbing row.  No date-\(1\) absorption upgrades those objects to full type shares and full conditional effects, while an all-exit reallocation proves the sharp frontier.  Guarded inference is uniform for the explicit saturated four-wave multinomial functional, including singular correlation; restricted-model efficiency remains open.
gap: Short-panel latent Markov reconstruction uses nonsingular terminal factors and positive transition arrays, while causal transition-independence work inherits those conditions; a common absorbing observed state creates identical terminal rows and structural zeros, and existing pointwise likelihood inference does not cover a data-dependent guarded recovery map on that face.
fill: The project supplies an explicit projector, row-sum, and pseudoinverse recovery formula with a full-fiber uniqueness theorem, exact boundary evidence, an analytic saturated-model gradient, and uniform multiplier coverage under observable buffered margins.
